correctness.rationale: Tree-incidence Gram determinants follow by Cauchy–Binet and unimodular cofactors. The 4-cycle characterization of forests in K_{2,q} yields two disjoint and exhaustive classes and exact combinatorial multiplicities at every rank. Binomial expectation representations, uniformly controlled Taylor remainders and square-root tilt bound yield the two-term Wills asymptotic and quantitative TV approximation. The extracted code reproduces 4,445 exact Gram determinants plus two direct convex-hull volumes; finitary checks are corroboration, not substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The strongest close published result is the general wedge-product intrinsic-volume identity of Joós–Lángi (credited as premise), which does not state the evaluated K_{2,q} spectrum, two-term Wills law or binomial total-variation approximation. Pohoata–Zhu studies hyperforest/Ehrhart and face combinatorics; Lotz et al. provides general concentration, not the claimed explicit limit. Retrieved earlier geometry work on complete-bipartite zonotope ellipsoids and cycle-zonotope intrinsic volumes concerns other metric invariants/graph structures. Indexed searches and accessible claims found no dominating theorem; historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The exact all-rank formula resolves the Euclidean Steiner parallel-volume polynomial for an infinite natural graph-zonotope family. The bridge-forest dominance explains the q^{3/2} weighting and gives a quantitative total-variation law, which is substantially more specific than generic concentration or a known spanning-tree count; it provides a reproducible model for high-dimensional intrinsic-volume profiles.
